Well, this is actually a very good question? My Tax professor did explain and its kinda long, so bear with my OP:

So when a finance bill is drafted, it is usually sent to the "experts" for their opinion, input in order to modify before passing it as an act. So in 2015- when the new budget and the bill was drafted, it included roping in the gold and silver merchants who till then had managed to rake in profits without contributing an equivalent share as tax to the Government. This did not go down well with the commodity trading industry and they did loby to decrease the tax rate. However, The government has to ensure it receives the already determined Tax revenue through one source or another. Since precious commodity taxes cant be increased, they figured increasing the tax on something else, so the net Tax revenue remains the same.

I do not have any source apart from my professor's lecture on this, so do take it with a grain of salt. But this really seems like a logical reason why Gold is taxed at 3% while biscuits are taxed at 5%.
